title: How I made the 3D assets for my cozy village game with Claude + Blender MCP
author: MartySalade
selftext:
Token Kingdom is a cozy village game where your Claude Code usage turns into resources. I made it solo in 2 weeks. Free to play.



What I learned about the asset pipeline:

* **Fully AI-generated meshes didn't fit.** Each one looked fine on its own, but put together they had no consistent style.
* **What worked: Claude assembles, artists' kits provide the parts.** Claude drives my live Blender through the Blender MCP server and builds models from KayKit low-poly packs. It reuses their texture atlas, so everything matches.
* **Gemini for concept boards only.** I generate a reference sheet, then the actual model is built in Blender from kit pieces.
* [**blender kiln**](https://github.com/elithril/blender-kiln) (open source) handled some assets end to end: cleanup, texturing, optimization, GLB export.
* **Small items** are modeled in Blender, then rendered to icons, so 3D and UI stay consistent.



Biggest lesson: AI works best as the hands, not the art director. A fixed art style + a kit of human-made parts beats prompting from scratch.

Happy to share details on the Blender MCP setup
